source.quote:
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of 
the United States of America, and in order to eliminate unnecessary adminis­
trative burdens and costs associated with the conversion of certain Federal 
powerplants to alternative sources of fuel, as required by the Powerplant and 
Industrial Fuel Use Act of 1978 (92 Stat. 3289), it is hereby ordered that 
Executive Order No. 12217 is revoked.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The whole order is one self-executing revocation: "it is hereby ordered that Executive Order No. 12217 is revoked." The act was complete on signing, August 11, 1983; the text sets no later effective date, and the order imposes no continuing duty. The exclusive reading is not relevant because no "until" or deadline is stated. Surviving consequence: EO 12217 stays revoked.

research_rationale:
EO 12437 (Fuel Use Prohibitions, Aug. 11, 1983, 48 FR 36801) is a one-sentence order whose only command is "it is hereby ordered that Executive Order No. 12217 is revoked." That is a self-executing act complete on signing, so the whole order ended on 1983-08-11 by performance on issue, with no continuing clause. The held text is the Federal Register printing of the whole order (heading, text, signature line "THE WHITE HOUSE, August 11, 1983" and filing line). The bounded machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register disposition notes) show no later instrument amending, revoking or superseding EO 12437; the one U.S. Code hit is the 42 U.S.C. 8373 note recording that EO 12217 was revoked by EO 12437.
